facts.statement: Stomatosuchus was an extinct neosuchian crocodylomorph that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) in the Bahariya Formation of Egypt.
facts.quote: Stomatosuchus (meaning "mouth crocodile") is an extinct stomatosuchid neosuchian from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) Bahariya Formation of Egypt.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Stomatosuchus was collected in Egypt in 1911 by the German paleontologist Ernst Stromer.
facts.quote: It was collected in Egypt during 1911 by the German paleontologist Ernst Stromer whilst on an expedition.

facts.statement: The specimen was delivered to the Munich Museum in 1922 but was destroyed during an Allied bombing raid on April 24–25, 1944.
facts.quote: It was delivered to the Munich Museum in 1922, and the museum was later destroyed by an Allied bombing raid on 24/25 April 1944.

facts.statement: Stomatosuchus grew to a length of 10 meters and had a skull up to 2 meters long featuring lid-like jaws lined with small, conical teeth.
facts.quote: It grew to a length of 10 m, and possessed a long, flattened skull with lid-like jaws that were lined with small, conical teeth, and the skull reached up to 2 m long.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the lower jaw of Stomatosuchus may have been toothless and supported a pelican-like throat pouch.
facts.quote: The mandible may have been toothless and perhaps even supported a pelican-like throat pouch.

facts.statement: The exact diet of Stomatosuchus remains largely unknown due to its unique skull structure.
facts.quote: Due to such a bizarre skull structure, much about the diet of S. inermis remains unknown.

facts.statement: Stomatosuchus likely inhabited the marshy lowlands of the modern-day Eastern Sahara Desert.
facts.quote: It is likely that S. inermis lived in the marshy lowlands of what is now the Eastern Sahara Desert.

facts.statement: Stomatosuchus inermis is the type and only known species of the genus Stomatosuchus.
facts.quote: The type and only species is S. inermis.

facts.statement: Stomatosuchus belongs to the family Stomatosuchidae.
Stomatosuchus lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: Stomatosuchus had a flattened skull with a long, flattened snout filled with small, conical teeth.
facts.quote: Su cráneo aplastado tenía un hocico largo y aplanado, que estaba lleno de dientes pequeños y cónicos.

facts.statement: The only known specimen, a large skull collected by Ernst Stromer in Egypt, was destroyed when the Munich Museum was bombed by Allied forces in 1944.
facts.quote: Lamentablemente el único ejemplar conocido, un cráneo de gran tamaño, que fue recolectado en la expedición a Egipto del paleontólogo alemán Ernst Stromer, fue destruido cuando el Museo de Múnich fue destruido durante un bombardeo aliado en 1944.

rejected.statement: Only photographs of the original specimen survive today because the fossil was destroyed in 1944.
rejected.quote: Currently, only photographs of the specimen remain.
